text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Communist Party chief Do Muoi has stressed the need for ths state to retain the major share of ownership in public sector businesses.
-- Health Minister Do Nguyen Phuong says Vietnam's health service is improving and surpassing that of other countries in the region with similar incomes.
-- The Japanese government has committed itself to building a three-kilometre bridge over the Red River in southern Hanoi.
-- A trial internet programme for Vietnam will be expanded from 300 users to 2000.
-- Saigon's Floating Hotel will leave Vietnam before March 20.
-- The Prime Minister has urged rapid completion of a feasibility study for a science park at Nghia Do, a suburb of Hanoi.
-- Senior government officials have opened a conference aimed at outlining Vietnam's cultural and ideological agenda for the next four years.
-- Former National Assembly Vice Chairman Huynh Cuong has died. He was 72.
-- Plans are being made for a $650 million satellite city outside Hanoi.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet will visit India later this week before travelling to Bangladesh.
